chapter: New York dance bands and Dorsey
title: Brief stint in Paul Whiteman's Woodbury Soap Hour group
summary: Freeman spends about a month in a small Whiteman radio band with Carl Kress, the Teagardens and Trumbauer, then goes with Tommy Dorsey.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: I got an offer then to go with Paul Whiteman just for a short spell. Carl Kress, the guitar player who died a few years back. I joined a little band in the Whiteman band. We were doing the a program which was called the Woodbury Soap Hour, which was a big radio show, and as a matter of fact, Johnny Mercer was writing material, songs, and singing in a group on the show, and in the band were Jack Teagarden, Charlie Teagarden, his brother, a marvelous trumpet player, let's see, Frank Trumbauer, C-melody saxophone. I am trying to think, Carl Kress, I played tenor, Carl Kress guitar and it seems to me the pianist was Roy Bargy from time to time. Remember the name, he was a fine writer, wonderful musician.

And so we had that little band and that was all we did, and then we made a few records with Whiteman. I was only with him maybe a month. And then I got the offer to go with Tommy Dorsey and went with Tommy.
